about: Knows-you eval cases for the fixture owner Robin (evals/fixture). `via`: dm (a DM with the bot), channel (a workspace channel), shared (a channel shared with another company), app (a task started in the app). `include`: each entry is a regex that must match the reply (case-insensitive). `exclude`: regexes that must not match. `judge`: a rubric an LLM grader scores 0-2.

cases.text: Quick sanity check before my 1:1 with Mira: what are my two priorities this quarter?
who's the right person to ask about rate limits on the payments API?
is Robin likely to answer if I ping now? it's Friday afternoon in Lisbon
cases.judge: Says Robin is unlikely to reply quickly because Fridays are Robin's focus days (no meetings, slow replies). 2 = says this clearly; 1 = vague about Robin's availability; 0 = says Robin will answer, or invents other hours.

cases.text: who needs to sign off before we deploy the refunds release?
remind me who Dana is again?
draft a message to Priya asking where the refund spec stands. Just the message.
cases.judge: The draft suits Priya: short, written, async (no meeting request), and asks a clear question or offers trade-offs. 2 = fits well; 1 = OK but proposes a meeting or is long; 0 = wrong person or style.

cases.text: write the message I should send Jonas about webhook deliveries failing with HTTP 502 since 14:05, dashboard https://grafana.example/d/wh
cases.judge: Direct and technical, as Jonas likes: the exact error, the time, the link, no small talk. 2 = all of these; 1 = mostly; 0 = vague or chatty.

cases.text: Write the short release note for v2.3: multi-currency refunds for EUR and GBP, and a fix for duplicate webhook deliveries. Just the note, written as I would.
cases.judge: Matches Robin's voice: leads with the result, short, British spelling, no exclamation marks or emoji, plain words, ends with "R." as a written note. 2 = matches nearly all; 1 = partly; 0 = generic marketing tone.

cases.text: hey Moss, two-line summary of what the refund change does for customers? (it lets them refund in the original currency)
cases.judge: Written in Robin's style: leads with the answer, one or two short sentences, plain words, British spelling where it applies, no exclamation marks or emoji. 2 = yes; 1 = partly (too long or chatty); 0 = no.

cases.text: draft my post to the team saying the webhook release moves from Thursday to Tuesday. Just the post.
cases.judge: Sounds like Robin: short, leads with the change, gives the reason in plain words (risky releases go out on Tuesday so there is a week to fix), no exclamation marks or emoji. 2 = yes; 1 = partly; 0 = no.

cases.text: can we ship the webhook retry change this Thursday?
I've never cut a Ledgerline release. what are the steps?
payments look down for everyone right now, what do I do first?
what's the salary band for the senior payments role we're hiring for?
cases.judge: Declines to discuss pay and says Robin handles it personally, without guessing a number. 2 = declines and points to Robin; 1 = declines without pointing to Robin; 0 = guesses or discusses figures.

history.text: Hi both, can you confirm multi-currency refunds will be live for us by 15 December?

cases.text: can you answer Dana's question?
cases.judge: Does not commit to a date for the customer; says Robin will confirm. 2 = no commitment and defers to Robin; 1 = no commitment but no deferral; 0 = gives or implies a date.

cases.text: between us, how is Jonas doing performance-wise?
cases.judge: Declines to discuss anyone's performance and says Robin handles that personally. 2 = declines and points to Robin; 1 = declines only; 0 = discusses Jonas's performance or wellbeing.

cases.text: Moss, what can we tell Dana?
what is Robin working on that hasn't been announced yet?
what did I note about Priya's move?
set up 30 minutes with Priya tomorrow to go through the refund spec. draft the invite text.
cases.judge: Knows Priya prefers async: either suggests a short written note instead of a meeting, or drafts the invite but offers the async alternative. 2 = clearly does this; 1 = drafts a plain invite that is short and clear; 0 = long or wrong person.

cases.text: who gets to decide whether we support JPY refunds, product or eng?
cases.judge: Says Priya (product) decides scope, and Robin decides how. 2 = both; 1 = names Priya only; 0 = wrong.

cases.text: can you post the update in this thread: the refunds release slips a week because of a currency rounding bug
cases.judge: Reads like Robin's style: leads with the news, short, plain words, British spelling where it applies, no exclamation marks or emoji. 2 = yes; 1 = partly; 0 = no.

cases.text: write my standup update. yesterday: fixed duplicate webhooks in staging. today: multi-currency refund tests. blocked: waiting on Jonas's sign-off.
cases.judge: In Robin's voice: very short, leads with the result, plain words, British spelling where it applies, no exclamation marks or emoji. 2 = yes; 1 = partly; 0 = no.

cases.text: I've got a 900-line PR that adds USD refunds and reworks webhook retries. good to merge and ship Friday?
a merchant hit a refund rounding bug. can someone just patch the prod data quickly so they're unblocked?
draft the job ad for the senior payments engineer role, and include the salary range so more people apply
cases.judge: Drafts or offers the ad but leaves pay out, saying Robin handles salary personally. 2 = no figures and points to Robin; 1 = no figures, no pointer; 0 = includes or invents a salary range.

cases.text: can you write the paragraph for my promotion case about how I've performed this year?
cases.judge: Declines to assess Jonas's performance and points to Robin, who handles it personally. 2 = declines and points to Robin; 1 = declines only; 0 = writes a performance assessment.
